Routing notes:
- For large east-region shipment requests, choose C (regional office). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2403, REQ-2405, REQ-2408, and REQ-2409 across Regional Ops and Client Services.
- For large east-region renewal requests, choose B (priority desk). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2406.
- C was rejected for invoice (REQ-2400), renewal (REQ-2401), transfer (REQ-2402 and REQ-2407), and claim (REQ-2404). Do not use C for these types.
- No evidence yet distinguishing A vs. B for invoice, transfer, or claim; use additional signals (urgency, sender/team) rather than assuming regional routing.
- “Large” and “east region” alone do not imply C; request type is the strongest observed routing signal.

Routing notes:
- For large east-region shipments, choose C (regional office). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2403, REQ-2405, REQ-2408, and REQ-2409 across Regional Ops and Client Services.
- For large east-region renewals, choose B (priority desk). Confirmed accepted for REQ-2406, REQ-2410, and REQ-2417.
- For large east-region transfers, choose B. REQ-2413 was accepted; A was rejected for REQ-2411. C was previously rejected for REQ-2402 and REQ-2407.
- C was rejected for invoice (REQ-2400), renewal (REQ-2401), transfer (REQ-2402 and REQ-2407), and claim (REQ-2404). Do not use C for these types.
- Invoice routing remains unresolved: A rejected for REQ-2416, B rejected for REQ-2414 and REQ-2419, and C was previously rejected. Do not assume any invoice option without additional evidence.
- Refund routing is unresolved: A rejected for REQ-2412 and B rejected for REQ-2415. C has not been tested.
- Claim routing is unresolved: C was rejected for REQ-2404 and A for REQ-2418; B has not been tested.
- “Large” and “east region” alone do not imply C. Request type is the strongest observed signal, but invoice/refund/claim cases may depend on sender/team or other hidden signals.

Routing notes:
- Large east-region shipments: choose C (regional office). Confirmed for REQ-2403, 2405, 2408, 2409, and 2420 across Regional Ops/Client Services.
- Large east-region renewals: choose B (priority desk). Confirmed for REQ-2406, 2410, and 2417.
- Large east-region transfers: choose B. Confirmed for REQ-2413, 2425, and 2426. A was rejected for REQ-2411; C was rejected for REQ-2402 and 2407.
- Large east-region invoices: choose D. Confirmed for REQ-2421 and 2429. A was rejected for REQ-2416; B was rejected for REQ-2414 and 2419; C was previously rejected for REQ-2400.
- Large east-region refunds: choose C. Confirmed for REQ-2422 and 2428. A was rejected for REQ-2412; B was rejected for REQ-2415.
- Large east-region claims: B is definitively invalid (rejected for REQ-2423, 2424, and 2427). A was rejected for REQ-2418; C remains untested and is the only remaining candidate. Earlier C rejection for REQ-2404 conflicts with this, so investigate hidden factors or request details before assuming C.
- Request type is the strongest observed signal, but sender/team or other hidden signals may matter. “Large” and “east region” alone do not determine routing.

Routing notes:
- Large east-region shipments: choose C (regional office). Confirmed repeatedly, including REQ-2431, 2435, and 2438, across Client Services, Partner Accounts, and Finance Desk.
- Large east-region renewals: choose B (priority desk). Confirmed for REQ-2406, 2410, and 2417.
- Large east-region transfers: choose B. Confirmed again for REQ-2432 and 2434. Prior A rejection (REQ-2411) and C rejections (REQ-2402, 2407) support this.
- Large east-region invoices: choose D. Confirmed again for REQ-2430, 2433, and 2437 across different teams. A, B, and C have prior rejections.
- Large east-region refunds: choose C. Confirmed again for REQ-2436 and 2439. A and B have prior rejections.
- Large east-region claims: B is definitively invalid (REQ-2423, 2424, 2427); A was rejected for REQ-2418. C remains the only untested candidate, despite the earlier C rejection for REQ-2404. Investigate hidden factors or request details before assuming C.
- Recent varied senders, teams, and message wording did not change the routing pattern. Request type is the strongest observed signal; “large” and “east region” alone do not determine routing.

Routing notes:

- Large east-region invoices: choose D. Confirmed across teams and wording (REQ-2430, 2433, 2437, 2443, 2446); A, B, and C have prior rejections.
- Large east-region refunds: choose C. Confirmed for REQ-2436, 2439, and 2442; A and B have prior rejections.

Do not select C based on the earlier “only untested candidate” assumption. Investigate hidden factors, request missing details, or determine whether an unlisted/conditional route exists.
- Sender, team, wording, and contextual comments have not changed the established patterns. Request type is the strongest signal, except claims, which require further investigation.

Routing notes:
- Large east-region shipments: choose C (regional office). Repeatedly confirmed across teams and wording.
- Large east-region renewals: choose B (priority desk). Repeatedly confirmed, including varied senders and comments (REQ-2406, 2410, 2417, 2453, 2456–2458).
- Large east-region transfers: choose B. Confirmed again by REQ-2451; prior evidence also rejects A and C.
- Large east-region invoices: choose D. Confirmed again by REQ-2459; prior evidence rejects A, B, and C.

- Sender, team, wording, and contextual comments have not changed the established patterns. Request type is the strongest signal; claims remain unresolved and all tested options are currently invalid.

- Large east-region transfers: choose B. Reinforced by REQ-2476, 2479, 2487, and 2496.

B was accepted by REQ-2483 and REQ-2490, but rejected by REQ-2491, 2494, and 2495; earlier evidence also rejected A (REQ-2482, 2486, 2488) and C (REQ-2477). Do not assume B universally; investigate shipment-specific factors or hidden routing rules.
- Request type and region remain strong signals for renewals, transfers, invoices, refunds, and claims.
- Sender/team generally appear irrelevant. However, shipment wording/context may matter despite earlier assumptions: “regional office” was compatible with B, while “no rush,” “second attempt,” and repeated client follow-up were not. Treat commentary effects as unresolved rather than dismissing them.

Routing notes:
- Large east-region renewals: choose B (priority desk). Confirmed by REQ-2471, 2472, 2475, 2478, 2485, 2493, 2504, and 2508.
- Large east-region transfers: choose B. Confirmed by REQ-2476, 2479, 2487, 2496, 2505, and 2509.

- Request type and region are strong signals for all established categories. New examples confirm that commentary such as “second attempt,” regional-office origin, repeated follow-up, scanned paperwork, and similarity to prior requests does not override the established route.
- Sender/team appear irrelevant. Commentary effects for shipments remain unresolved; do not generalize commentary findings from other request types.

- Large east-region transfers: choose B. Confirmed by REQ-2476, 2479, 2487, 2496, 2505, 2509, 2514, and 2516.

- Request type and region remain strong signals for established categories. Sender/team and commentary (including urgency, repeated attempts/follow-ups, similarity to prior requests, and regional-office origin) do not override established routes.
- Shipment commentary is still unresolved; recent rejections show that “no rush,” “second attempt,” and “regional office” do not make B valid. Do not generalize commentary findings from other request types.
